Lines.Text: CLICK. CREEEAK—
The steel door P had almost torn from its hinges now opened with an unnervingly slow, measured movement.
In the bleak, colorless boardroom, the executives were clinking cognac glasses to celebrate the disposal of their troublesome rejects. Every head turned toward the door.
P stood there.
The defeated man who had staggered in, panting with anger and fear, was gone.
Cold rooftop snow melted on his filthy jacket,
but his eyes were colder still, perfectly calm.
He looked like a demon that had crawled out of hell—his stillness made the threat in him all the more chilling.
Ignoring the executives' irritated stares, P dragged his wet shoes across the floor to the obsidian table.
He took a large, crumpled envelope from inside his jacket and tossed it down.
THUMP. PATTER—
The envelope split open. Documents spilled across the cold tabletop.
A receipt for the return of his apartment's lease deposit. Statements confirming the sale of his stocks. His personal seal.
And... a deed assigning all future royalty income from the many hit songs he had released under S-Tier.
(in a dry, hollow voice) Four hundred eighty million won. Every last won accounted for.
That's their termination penalty paid in full. Release my girls from their contracts. Today.
(looking up from the papers, her eyes widening slightly) You... Have you lost your mind? You're throwing your entire life down the drain.
Yeah. Pretty cheap, considering what you did to my girls. Treating them like toys.
(slamming the table) Stop right there, P! Fine, terminate their contracts. But what about yours?
You still owe us two years under your exclusive producer agreement.
You're the face of S-Tier! Did you consider what walking out would do to our share price? Our roster?!
They had been happy to throw the girls away as garbage. But P, their golden goose, could never be allowed to leave. Their greed was sickening.
(snarling, veins bulging) This crazy bastard's got delusions of grandeur!
Your songs were hits because of our money and our infrastructure! What the hell can you do on your own with those branded little trash bitches?
Want us to sue you for breach of contract too? Keep you buried in debt for the rest of your life?!
(restraining Kim, speaking quietly to P) Face reality, P. You're a genius. Your talent's too valuable to waste on damaged goods.
Be the lead director on my first project as Chief Producer.
I'll overlook this little insurrection. We'll forget that envelope was ever here. Don't pack your bags. Sit down where you belong.
Coaxing, threats, and the sweet promise of compromise.
Most people would have buckled beneath that much money and power.
P leaned forward, planted both hands on the obsidian table, and looked from Kim to Joo-hee.
His bloodied lips twisted into a strange smile.
You didn't read all the papers, did you?
My own termination penalty's in there too. I cashed out everything.
That fucking leash you've had around my throat? I paid for the privilege of tearing it off myself.
Wh... what...?
The girls and I don't owe S-Tier a single won anymore.
I'd rather crawl through the mud and build them a stage myself than lose them playing by your sick rules.
So keep your filthy hands off my girls. For good.
His conviction did not waver. It bordered on madness.

The executives had believed that money and power could control anything. For the first time, a chill ran through them. Here was a monster beyond their control, willing to give up a fortune and walk straight into ruin.
(shouting, his voice shaking) Fine! Get out! I'll make damn sure you see what this industry does to you! We'll grind you into the dirt and bury you alive!
(opening the boardroom door, his voice cold) Whether I starve out there or end up selling my soul to the devil in hell... that's my business.
With that final, chilling remark, P walked through the steel door without looking back.
The world called the girls defective and threw them in the trash.
He threw away the sick bargain it called adult reason. For the girls who trusted him completely, he would become a bloodied shield and walk into hell.
Curses and shattering glass followed him down the hall.
He never broke stride, marching like a martyr who had chosen to carry his own cross.
WHIRRR—
The stark white basement practice room again.
The girls had not moved. They huddled on the floor, arms around one another, waiting for him.
When the door opened and P stepped inside in his dirt-stained jacket, five desperate faces turned toward him.
(her voice trembling) P... What did Chief Producer Joo-hee... say...? Is this really how it ends for us...?
P walked over to them and lowered himself to the floor.
He gently eased Ria's hand away from the thigh she had pinched bloody, then wiped Jiwoo's tear-soaked cheek with his rough palm.
Stop crying.
Everybody up. Pack your things. Now.
(staring blankly) Pack up...? What about the penalty... Are you saying we're being thrown out...?
Everyone held their breath, watching his mouth.
P gave them a smile that was both warm and unshakable.
No. We're busting out of this rotten factory ourselves.
I've paid it all off. From now on, you're my artists. You don't belong to S-Tier's assembly line anymore.
(her eyes going wide) Huh...? P, all that debt... How did you even...?
You don't need to worry about that. Just be ready to sing and dance.
We might have to take the long way around... but I swear I'll put you on the brightest stage in the world.
For the girls trapped in that pitch-black despair, his declaration was a lifeline. Salvation.
Their suppressed sobs broke loose all at once.
All five collapsed into his arms, crying openly.
P wrapped his snow-damp, dirt-streaked arms around their small shoulders and held them fiercely. They had trusted him enough to leap with him into the unknown.
Their hot tears soaked his old jacket.
Tomorrow, they would face the streets and a world that wanted nothing to do with them.
But here, now, sharing their warmth in that cramped practice room,
it seemed as though even this vast, cruel world could not break them.
